summary: A cheap, shape-disjoint and rules-clean test of load hoisting at decode_32 that can only be read from the post-norm kernel row (its headline effect is about 0.15% of the geomean), so proceed without companions, ideally after its bs<32 sibling post-norm-combine-hoisted-slot-loads has shown whether hoisting moves that kernel at all.
justification: Mechanism: master's _post_norm_combine_kernel puts each of the 8 slots under a scalar 'if eid >= 0', which serialises up to 8 dependent L2 round trips per program. y was just written by the w2 Marlin, is about 2 MB at bs=32 and sits in L2, so the kernel is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, and issuing every masked load up front plausibly cuts it to one or two round trips. Profile support: at bs=32 SGLang's _post_expert_norm_weighted_sum_kernel is 3.6-4.5 us across jobs (3.6 in 3cabc739 profile 2, 4.0 in FINDINGS, 4.5 in the hypothesis), and the old serial Triton kernel measured 3.8 us there (post-norm-triton-all-m, job 2ec5387f). So the new ingredient really is the hoisting, and about 2.5 us is a reasonable target. The expected directions are consistent: only decode_32 moves, and every other shape's code path is byte-identical. Weakest link: the payoff is about 1-2 us on a roughly 200 us shape that carries 1/6 of the geomean, about 0.15% of the headline, far inside the ±1.5% CI. decode_32's Marlin time is seed-noisy (169-190 us), and the SGLang post-norm row itself drifts about 0.9 us between jobs, which is as large as the expected saving. A result is therefore readable only as the new kernel's row against the 3.6-4.5 us band, and anything above about 3 us is ambiguous. Two smaller doubts: ptxas may already have if-converted and hoisted part of the serial kernel, and at bs=32 under skewed routing the mean number of local slots per token may be only about 2-4, which shrinks the serial chain that hoisting removes. Grid (32,) also leaves about 100 SMs idle, so per-program latency still dominates after the change.
confounders: post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: defines the math and the bs<32 kernel that this one copies; decode_32 still runs SGLang's kernel on master, so it does not confound the decode_32 measurement, it only sets the code template.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: _align_small_kernel produces the local_ids the new kernel reads at bs=32; it is upstream in the same graph but its time is a separate profile row, so it cannot leak into the post-norm row.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm and align-parallel-per-expert-verify: act only at num_tokens >= 128 / > 32 and do not touch decode_32; no interaction.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: fixes the y layout [M, 8, H] with uninitialised remote rows, which the masked loads must respect; needed, but not a confounder of timing.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change is a separate kernel used only at bs=32, so its own profile row attributes it. The control already exists: SGLang's kernel row at bs=32 in this job's own baseline profile and in 3cabc739, plus the old serial Triton kernel at 3.8 us in post-norm-triton-all-m. Reverting any landed hypothesis would not change what the decode_32 post-norm kernel sees. A serial-vs-hoisted control at bs=32 would duplicate post-norm-triton-all-m. The cheapest way to tighten the read is an in-run, untimed microbenchmark in prepare(): time the new kernel, master's serial _post_norm_combine_kernel and SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum on one synthetic [32, 8, 4096] y with a fixed synthetic routing (CUDA events, about 200 iterations each), and print the three medians to the log. That gives a same-GPU A/B without spending a check. Sequencing matters more than companions: run this after post-norm-combine-hoisted-slot-loads. If the sibling's _post_norm_combine_kernel row does not drop, the mechanism has failed and this run can be dropped.
rules_flags: None blocking. The branch is on num_tokens (shape) only and is graph-safe. Remote slots are masked, never read, and a fully-remote token yields exact zeros (g forced to 0, v = 0, so no NaN from rsqrt(eps)). Math is fp32 with bf16 output and the weights are not re-quantised. The prepare() warm-up uses dummy tensors and caches nothing derived from inputs.
Make sure the warm-up in prepare() uses dummy ids/y only (not data) and that kernel_fn still allocates out with torch.empty inside the graph, as master's small-M path does.
bs=33 must stay on SGLang's path (the elif is == 32, not <= 32 with a different threshold); confirm SMALL_M_POST_NORM is not edited.
open_questions: At bs=32 under the skewed ep8 routing, how many local slots does a token have on average? If it is about 2, the serial chain is short and hoisting buys little.

Did ptxas already if-convert the serial kernel's loads? Check its SASS for predicated LDGs ahead of the reductions. If so, the 3.8 us serial time is already 'hoisted' and the floor is elsewhere (launch, grid of 32).
Would a 2-D grid (32 tokens x 2-4 H-chunks, with sum-of-squares needing the full row) or one program per (token, slot) with an atomic combine beat hoisting, given that only 32 of 132 SMs are busy?
If both this and the sibling win, restack them as a single hoisted kernel for bs<=32 and retire the separate decode32 branch.
